name: Arithmetic with congruences
formula: a \equiv b \pmod m \implies a + c \equiv b + c, \quad ac \equiv bc, \quad a^k \equiv b^k \pmod m
whenToUse: Find a remainder by replacing each number by something smaller or negative with the same remainder before adding, multiplying or raising to a power.
pitfall: You may not divide both sides of a congruence freely: $2a \equiv 2b \pmod{6}$ only gives $a \equiv b \pmod{3}$. Divide only by numbers coprime to the modulus.
